html:
The British Empire was the set of colonies, protectorates, dominions and other lands ruled from Britain. It grew from the early 1600s, and at its height around 1920 it covered about a quarter of the world's land and people, the largest empire in history.

Its main phases:

  • The Atlantic, 1600s and 1700s. Colonies in North America, sugar islands in the Caribbean worked by enslaved Africans, and forts in West Africa such as Elmina later on. The thirteen colonies broke away in 1776.
  • India and Asia. The East India Company took Bengal after 1757 and then most of India; the Crown took over as the British Raj in 1858. Ceylon, Burma, Malaya and Hong Kong followed.
  • Settlers and Africa, 1800s. Canada, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa filled with British settlers and became self-governing dominions. In the scramble for Africa Britain took Nigeria, with the kingdom of Benin in 1897, Kenya and much else. It conquered the Zulu Kingdom in 1879, despite defeat at Isandlwana.

Britain banned the slave trade in 1807 and ended slavery in most colonies with the Slavery Abolition Act of 1833. The Royal Navy, the pound and British trade held the empire together and spread English around the world.

The world wars drained Britain. India and Pakistan became independent in 1947, and most colonies in Africa and the Caribbean in the 1950s and 1960s, the age of decolonisation. The handover of Hong Kong to China in 1997 is usually taken as the end. Most former colonies joined the Commonwealth.
